chunks: Techniques to reduce power consumption. The question: What can you do to decrease power consumption?
Chip power comes from two places. Switching power is spent when circuits flip between 0 and 1. Leakage power is a trickle that flows even when nothing flips.
Every low-power technique attacks one of these. The biggest wins are not doing the work at all, running at a lower voltage, and switching off whatever is idle.
Software matters as much as hardware, because it decides when parts sleep.
Think of saving energy in a house. You turn off lights in empty rooms. That is clock gating, which stops idle circuits from switching, and power gating, which cuts their supply.
You lower the thermostat when you need less heat, which is lowering voltage and speed. You avoid unnecessary trips to the store, which is avoiding memory accesses.
You also fix the drafty windows, which is leakage. A trip to the far store costs far more fuel than a task at home.
Each branch is one term of the power equation.
Voltage and activity usually give the biggest savings; leakage management matters more as devices shrink and as products spend more time idle.
Dynamic power: switching power, alpha C V squared f (how often wires flip, how much charge they hold, voltage squared, clock frequency).
Leakage: current that flows through transistors (the chip's tiny switches) even when they are idle. Clock gating: stopping the clock to idle circuits so they do not switch.
Power gating: cutting the supply to an idle block, which also removes its leakage. DVFS: lowering voltage and frequency together when the load is light.
Duty cycling: alternating short active bursts with long sleeps.
A small microcontroller draws 10 milliamps when active and 2 microamps when asleep. Active all the time, it averages 10 milliamps.
If it is active only 1% of the time, the average is 0. 01 times 10 000 micro A plus 0. 99 times 2 micro A about 102 micro A . That is about 100 times less.
A coin cell holding 220 milliamp hours (milliamp-hours) of charge then lasts about 90 days instead of 22 hours. That is the whole idea.
"I'd go through the power equation.

Dynamic power is activity times capacitance times V squared times frequency, so: lower voltage and frequency with DVFS and multiple voltage domains; cut activity with clock gating, operand isolation and architectural choices that avoid work; reduce capacitance with smaller devices and shorter wires.
For leakage use high-Vt cells, and power gating with retention for idle blocks. Then system-level: deep sleep states, race-to-idle and efficient regulators."
